implemented: Native structure revision guards, ordered generated-ID results, frozen template transform overrides, and bounded spawn payload preparation.
Prepare entity handles and explicit-ID Jolt bodies outside broadphase; validate candidate custom/global references before publishing live membership.
Retain removed body/entity allocations until component commit; remove born resources and restore ID allocators on preparation failure.
Store live birth recipe and initial transform provenance; never recycle committed generated public IDs.
Refresh character support after structural publication and include character-owned state in the rollback checkpoint.
Reject portable snapshot export after any structural commit until topology-aware save restoration is implemented.

native_lifecycle_checks: Failed multi-spawn with dangling recipe reference preserves topology, component revision and generated ID sequence.
Subsequent dynamic physics matches a clean control after rejected preparation.
Spawned native components are queryable; incoming references reject removal without revision changes.
Removed IDs are not reused; repeated create/remove cycles return live membership to baseline.
Removing a platform immediately clears character support and prevents a jump from deleted support.
Spawned kinematic bodies execute target motion; bodyless props do not add physics bodies.
Stale revisions, duplicate removals and unsupported authored-entity removal reject atomically.
Save export rejects even after all generated props are removed, preventing silent allocator-history loss.

limits: Native paused-boundary prototype only; no RPC/C# lifecycle methods or multi-tick structural rollback integration.
Removal currently accepts previously spawned root props only, not arbitrary authored entities.
Component reference repair cannot yet be submitted in the same structural request.
Topology-bearing portable saves remain explicitly unavailable.
Retired bodies occupy capacity until commit; replacement requires temporary headroom under the existing 4096-body limit.
No injected failure after physics publication; checkpoint restore path is inspected but not fault-injection qualified here.
No production-scale performance or cross-platform determinism claim.
